A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaRank by the same authors. All 16 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and language model-merging results, singular-component loss analyses, learned masks and component ablations in Sections 4 and 6 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional oracle experiments, rank-selection ablations, router comparisons and computational measurements in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The entropy objective, binary singular-component masks, straight-through estimator and joint coefficient adaptation remain. v2 adds a TSV-M integration that whitens concatenated singular-vector matrices before mask adaptation (Section 6.1 and Algorithm 2), plus an optional composition with Representation Surgery.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nested sets of 8, 14 and 20 vision classification tasks and the same seven GLUE tasks. v2 relocates and expands dataset descriptions; the added analyses introduce no new datasets, domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates Twin-Merging and WEMoE, adds TSV-M to the NLP comparisons, and adds TSV-M+AdaMerging to vision comparisons. v1's AdaMerging-with-Surgery comparator is omitted, while v2 evaluates AdaRank followed by Surgery. Original vision comparators, including both Consensus variants, remain in the detailed appendix tables despite omissions from main-text summaries.

E3.justification: v2 adds supervised cross-entropy versus unsupervised entropy optimization from a common top-16% initialization, restricted versus full-spectrum selection, and intrinsic-rank truncation controls. Router comparisons use a shared unlabeled split and adaptation budget, and computational comparisons measure parameter counts and execution time. These are additional evaluation protocols; the original backbones, optimizer and stated learning rates remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's interference analysis, mask visualization and coefficient/mask ablation, v2 tests whether supervised mask optimization can recover individual-model loss, whether bottom components help, and whether intrinsic-rank truncation suffices (Figures 4-5 and Table 4). It extends the component ablation to TSV-M and adds computational-cost and Surgery-compatibility analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed identifiers, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added tables and plots retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial TSV-M, router, Surgery and diagnostic results. Reported CART+AdaRank averages change from 0.7417 to 0.7547 for RoBERTa and from 0.6485 to 0.6587 for GPT-2 (v1 Tables 2-3; v2 Tables 15-16). Existing detailed vision rows remain unchanged. Some new summary and appendix values disagree, so the revised reporting does not establish verified same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 changes the formally stated mask length from d to min(d,d'), correcting the dimension for rectangular weight matrices. The core equations and 95%-spectral-energy rank definition remain; renaming effective rank to intrinsic rank introduces no new mathematical measure. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 replaces v1's headline state-of-the-art and nearly-1%-gap assertions with claims of consistent improvement and substantial gap reduction. Its introduction additionally claims competitive router performance without model-size growth and compatibility with post-calibration. The central contribution of adaptive singular-component selection is retained.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the oracle experiment as evidence that component selection can recover individual-model performance. It conjectures that bottom components preserve fine details with less interference, explains why matching intrinsic rank alone is insufficient, and attributes Surgery's complementary gains to correcting the residual gap from entropy-only adaptation. These substantially extend v1's pruning and rank-variation interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 adds pseudocode, selected CART initialization values of lambda=2.3 and top-16%, TSV-M initialization information, dataset descriptions and SVD/adaptation timings. Existing STE temperature, optimizer settings, hardware and checkpoint sources are largely retained. v1's code-release statement and repository link are omitted; this establishes removal of access information, not withdrawal of the code itself.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning relative to routers, compression methods and post-calibration, adding the MoErging survey, Surgeryv2 and newer adaptation references. It replaces the effective-rank citation with PCA references and removes several earlier merging/pruning references. Its principal novelty relative to heuristic top-k selection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, vision and language experiments are consolidated under Main Results, and the appendices are reorganized into algorithm details, experimental setup and additional results. Terminology and explanatory subheadings are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column layout, combines and redraws interference plots, adds diagnostic and computational displays, and removes radar charts while retaining their tabulated results. Detailed NLP tables move to the appendix with a compact main-text summary. The six-panel TA/CART mask figure becomes a three-row full-spectrum appendix visualization.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the explanation of AdaRank through oracle, selection-range and intrinsic-rank controls, and substantiates efficiency with router comparisons and timing measurements. However, the code-access disclosure is removed and new numerical inconsistencies weaken comparative reporting: TSV-M+AdaMerging's 14-task ViT-B/32 entries in Table 11 average about 87.36%, whereas Table 1 reports 84.5%. The added analytical support and clearer organization provide a net improvement, but these reporting and reproducibility drawbacks limit its overall magnitude.
